blocks.text: Pesticides are chemicals used to kill or control pests such as insects, weeds or fungi. They protect crops from damage, prevent food loss and help ensure a stable food supply. They are classified by their target pest into insecticides, herbicides and fungicides.

blocks.caption: Kinds of pesticide (from the text)
rows: Act as neurotoxins on the insect's nervous system, causing paralysis and death
Some inhibit enzymes so essential amino acids cannot be made; others disrupt electron transport so the weed cannot photosynthesise
Attack the cell's integrity; for example they block ergosterol synthesis, so the fungal membrane leaks and the cell dies

blocks.title: Zinc phosphide is not a fungicide
blocks.text: The book lists zinc phosphide among common fungicides; it is used as a rodenticide (rat poison). Also, only some fungicides (such as triazoles) act on ergosterol synthesis; strobilurins instead block energy production in fungal cells. Flagged for review.

Pesticides play a key role in modern food programmes. They protect plants from pests and diseases and increase crop yields, reduce the risk of epidemics and improve human health, and contribute to food security worldwide. But they can also harm health, being carcinogenic and neurotoxic. Beneficial insects, birds and aquatic organisms can be affected; runoff from fields can contaminate water sources; and non-target species such as pollinating bees can be harmed (neonicotinoids have been reported to be linked to 'colony collapse disorder' in honeybees). Over time pests can become resistant to a pesticide, which forces the use of more toxic pesticides with further environmental and health risks.

blocks.prompt: Give one benefit and one risk of using pesticides.
blocks.explanation: Benefit: they protect crops and increase yields (food security). Risk: for example, they can harm non-target species such as bees, contaminate water, or lead to resistant pests.

items: Insecticides: nervous system; herbicides: amino acid synthesis or photosynthesis; fungicides: cell membrane.
Benefits: yields, food security; risks: health, bees, water, resistance.
